questions.a: (n - 2) × 180 = 130n gives 50n = 360 and n = 7.2, not a whole number: no.

questions.a: Exterior e, interior 4e: 5e = 180, e = 36°, so n = 10

questions.q: The angle sum of a pentagon is:
One interior angle of a regular hexagon
Big question: is there a rule for the angle sum of any polygon?
questions.a: Yes: (n - 2) × 180°, because it splits into n - 2 triangles from one vertex.

questions.q: The exterior angles of any polygon add up to:
The exterior angle of a regular 12-gon
Big question: why do exterior angles always add up to 360°?
questions.a: Walking round the shape you turn through each exterior angle and end facing the way you started: one full turn.
